mfrmr: Many-Facet Ordered-Response Modeling in R

Source: R/help_workflow_methods.R, R/mfrmr-package.R
mfrmr-package.Rd

Analyze ordered ratings involving raters, tasks and criteria. The package provides measurement models, observed-score assessment planning and rater feedback. Choose a route from the question; these are not compulsory stages of a single analysis.

Five-question workflow map

Question Start with Inspect next
Person abilities and facet effects describe_mfrm_data(), fit_mfrm() summary(fit)$decision, estimate tables
Rater/task counts and score weights mfrm_g_study(), mfrm_d_study() Declared design, G/Phi, interval status
Ratings or rater patterns needing review diagnose_mfrm(), estimate_bias(), analyze_dff() Diagnostic target, counts, availability reasons
Observed rater score agreement interrater_agreement_table() or pairwise agreement helpers Matched units, agreement definition, denominator
Scoring new Persons on a fixed calibration predict_mfrm_units() or mfrm_calibration_workflow Conditional EAP/SD, prior, source checks

Observed agreement and G-Study/D-Study planning use raw ratings directly and do not establish MFRM fit; rater severity separation is distinct from inter-rater agreement. See vignette("mfrmr-workflow", package = "mfrmr") and mfrmr_output_guide() for step-by-step routes.

Choose an analysis route

  • Measurement: describe_mfrm_data() reviews rating rows and the design; fit_mfrm() estimates Person abilities, facet effects and category steps within the selected model's scope. Read summary(fit)$decision before interpreting the estimates. The example below starts with bundled ratings.

  • Assessment planning: mfrm_g_study() estimates observed-score variance components; mfrm_d_study() compares specified rater/task plans. Neither requires an MFRM fit. G/Phi refer to the declared score and replication plan.

  • Rater feedback: interrater_agreement_table() describes agreement, diagnose_mfrm() reviews supported response-fit diagnostics, and estimate_bias() / analyze_dff() address specified interaction/group questions. Severity, agreement and fit are different targets.

Learning and reference

Use vignette("mfrmr-workflow", package = "mfrmr") for a first analysis and importing your own ratings. The model-choice, G-theory, visual-diagnostics and reporting tutorials address the corresponding decisions; list installed tutorials with vignette(package = "mfrmr").

mfrmr_workflow_methods connects the main result objects. Use mfrmr_methods_reference to locate definitions and methodological sources, or mfrmr_output_guide() for the five central routes. Use mfrmr_output_guide("all") to find specialist tables, figures or exports. Function help gives the installed version's arguments, calculations and limitations. Additional packages are required only by the features that name them in their help. Cite citation("mfrmr") and the methods actually used.

Saved analyses

Keep complete result objects with base::saveRDS() and record the package version and analysis settings. Reopening with base::readRDS() does not update calculations. mfrmr_compatibility_layer distinguishes redisplaying, recomputing derived results and refitting when updating older analyses. For scoring against a portable fixed calibration, use mfrm_calibration_workflow; this is a different artifact from a saved fit.

Interpretation

Model, estimator, score coding, assignment and uncertainty assumptions must match the intended use. A returned estimate, numerical convergence and an available interval are separate results. The specialist help and returned status/reason fields state the applicable restrictions; a review flag is not an automatic judgment of rater quality or fairness.

Examples 

# Load the package
library(mfrmr)

# Load example ratings and look at the first six rows
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
head(ratings)
#>                Study Person Rater    Criterion Score Group
#> 1 OperationalExample   P001   R01     Language     4     A
#> 2 OperationalExample   P001   R01 Organization     2     A
#> 3 OperationalExample   P001   R02      Content     4     A
#> 4 OperationalExample   P001   R02     Language     3     A
#> 5 OperationalExample   P001   R02 Organization     2     A
#> 6 OperationalExample   P002   R01      Content     3     A

# Fit the model
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

# Read the interpretation status before examining or plotting estimates
results <- summary(fit)
results$decision
#>                                                           Interpretation
#> 1 Fit-readiness requirements satisfied; formal precision review required
#>   FormalInference FitReadiness
#> 1              No        ready
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Why
#> 1 Formal precision support has not been evaluated. These checks assess numerical readiness and the requested precision method under the specified model; they do not establish model adequacy or finite-sample coverage for this design.
#>                                                                                                                                                   NextAction
#> 1 Run `diagnose_mfrm()` and pass its result as `diagnostics =` to evaluate formal precision support; fit readiness alone is not a formal-inference decision.
results$person_overview # One row summarizing person ability estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   Persons DistributionN ReviewExcludedExtremeE…¹ EstimateUse   Mean    SD Median
#>     <int>         <int>                    <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1      48            48                        0 source_fit… -0.155 0.824 -0.208
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​ReviewExcludedExtremeEAPs
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: Min <dbl>, Max <dbl>, Span <dbl>, MeanPosteriorSD <dbl>
results$facet_overview  # One row per facet: number of levels, mean, SD, range
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   Facet     Levels MeanEstimate SDEstimate MinEstimate MaxEstimate  Span
#>   <chr>      <int>        <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Criterion      3     0             0.302      -0.344       0.224 0.568
#> 2 Rater          6    -4.64e-18      0.399      -0.606       0.412 1.02 

# Plot the results (Wright map) within the reported interpretation limits
plot(fit)
